fields.corePath: Fee Khata is for a tuition teacher running batches out of her flat. Step 1, she opens the site. The main screen is a sign-in box, but under it there is a button that says See a demo batch — no sign in, and that button opens a full working batch with eighteen made-up students and three months of fee history. Step 2, inside the batch she sees a table: student name, monthly fee, paid till month, balance. Step 3, she taps Mark paid on a student's row, picks the month and the mode — cash, UPI or cheque — and saves. Step 4, the balance in that row drops and the total at the top updates. Step 5, she taps Receipt on that row and a receipt opens with the batch name, the student, the month and the amount, which she can save as an image and send on WhatsApp. Step 6, she taps Who has not paid and gets only the defaulters for the current month, with a pre-written reminder message per parent. Everything in steps 2 to 6 works inside the demo batch. To keep her own students she signs in with a Google account, but nothing in the path above needs that.
fields.knownGaps: The demo batch resets every time you reload — anything you mark paid in it is gone, which surprises people and I should put a line saying so. For a real batch, sign-in is Google only; two of the teachers I showed it to do not have a Gmail they remember the password for, and that has genuinely cost me two users, so phone OTP is the next thing I am building. Receipts are generated client-side as a PNG and on older Android phones the text renders slightly clipped at the bottom edge. There is no part payment — a month is either paid or not, and one teacher takes ₹500 now and ₹500 later, so she has been marking the month paid early and remembering the rest in her head, which defeats the point. No fee history export. No multiple batches per teacher yet; she has three batches and is using three Google accounts, which is ridiculous and I know it. Marking paid, the receipt and the defaulter list all work.

notes: Borderline, committed to pass. A strict reviewer could call the entry point a login wall and fail `core-path-works`, since the first thing on the page is Sign in with Google. But the demo button sits immediately under it, is visible in the render, and carries the full named path with no account — so a stranger really can do the job start to finish. The gap list is unusually candid and everything in it sits off the path.
